topic: Mechanics - Net Force and Newton's Second Law
question:
The net force acting on an object on a horizontal surface is always …

A in the direction of motion of the object.
B in the direction of acceleration of the object.
C zero when the object moves at constant acceleration.
D increasing when the object moves at constant acceleration.
memo:
B $\checkmark\checkmark$

*Rationale: By Newton's second law, $F_{\text{net}} = ma$, so the net force on an object is always in the same direction as its acceleration. The net force need not act in the direction of motion, and when the acceleration is constant the net force is constant (neither zero nor increasing).*
